newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones rises on Fortune article.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones rises on Fortune article.

text.p: Shares of Dow Jones & Co Inc rose Monday after a Fortune Magazine article said younger members of the family who control the media company are pushing management to improve shareholder value, analysts said.
Dow Jones gained 3-1/8 to 38-7/8 in afternoon trading.

The Fortune article said Elisabeth Goth, great-great grandchild of Clarence Barron, has consulted financier Warren Buffett and media investment banking firm Allen & Co about whether her $23 million stake in Dow Jones is worth holding and what can be done to move the share price higher.
Clarence Barron bought the Wall Street Journal and the Dow Jones News Service in 1902.
A Dow Jones spokesman could not be immediately reached to comment.
A Dow Jones spokesman later said the company does not comment on market activity or rumors. The company, however, said it was aware of the Fortune article.

Dow Jones Chairman Peter Kann said in a statement that "the most relevant information in that article is near the end, where it states that the Bancroft family as a whole and its trustees are unified in their commitment to continued ownership of Dow Jones."
The Bancroft family owns less than 50 percent of Dow Jones' common stock, but has almost 70 percent voting control in the company, Dow Jones spokesman Roger May said.

The Bancrofts are heirs to Barron's ownership stake of Dow Jones. Bettina Bancroft, one of nine great-grandchildren of Barron, died last May. When Bancroft died, her daughter, Elisabeth Goth, assumed control of her mother's holdings.
Goth received 700,000 shares of stock and also is the beneficiary of "hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of Dow Jones shares," the article said.
